grade.rationale: The stylesheet is compact and generally coherent, but its focus styling can leave keyboard-focused tree rows without any visible focus indicator.

summary: One medium-severity accessibility correctness issue was identified: the default focus outline is removed from every tree row, while the replacement is limited to rows that also have the separate `active` class. No test coverage conclusions were drawn because coverage data is unavailable.

grade.rationale: Most selectors are internally consistent, but visible keyboard focus depends on application state synchronizing `active` with focus.
Selectors and design tokens are reasonably organized, although densely packed declarations make changes and reviews somewhat harder.
Class names communicate intent, but the relationship between the `active` state and focus styling is implicit and fragile.
Error handling is largely inapplicable to this static stylesheet, and no relevant fallback defect was confirmed.
State-based selectors are amenable to interaction and visual testing; actual coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was provided.

findings.title: Keyboard focus can be invisible on non-active tree rows
findings.description: The rule removes the browser focus outline from every `.tree-row`, but the replacement `:focus-visible` outline applies only when the same row also has `.active`. If focus and active state ever diverge—for example during programmatic focus, initialization, or a state-update delay—the focused control has no visible focus indication.
findings.recommendation: Apply the replacement outline to `.tree-row:focus-visible` unconditionally. If active rows require distinct styling, add that styling separately without making basic focus visibility depend on the `active` class.
